learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of xslt template rules and explain at least one listed subtopic.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xslt template rules within XSLT — XML Transformation. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XSLT Template Rules matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about match patterns, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XSLT applies template rules to a source tree and builds a result tree or serialized output. XPath expressions select source nodes; explicit templates make transformation behavior easier to test than assumptions about processor defaults.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Match patterns; Template selection; The document-root template; Built-in template rules; Template precedence. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: XSLT Template Rules
content_blocks.expected_output: Against the sample catalog, an XSLT 1.0 processor can produce an HTML unordered list containing the product names.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Run a stylesheet with a known sample input and compare the output structurally where possible. XSLT 1.0 is widely implemented by browsers and libraries; XSLT 2.0/3.0 features require a processor that supports those versions.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: This stylesheet targets XSLT 1.0. XSLT 2.0/3.0 syntax and streaming features require a processor that implements the relevant version.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Record the exact processor and version: specification support is not universal, especially for XSD 1.1, XPath 2.0/3.1, XQuery, and XSLT 2.0/3.0.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Match patterns”. Then add one boundary case involving “Template selection”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
